/**
 * Published novels, measured.
 *
 * Generated by `tools/harvest-reference.ts` — do not edit by hand. Every number
 * here was produced by running this application's own extractor over the actual
 * text of a public-domain book from Project Gutenberg, so a manuscript compared
 * against them is being compared against arithmetic rather than against
 * received wisdom about how novels are written.
 *
 * Only the numbers are kept. No prose is stored or shipped: a mean sentence
 * length is a fact about a book, not a piece of it.
 *
 * Public domain only, which shapes what is here. There is no contemporary
 * genre fiction, no living writer, and nothing after the 1920s — those books
 * cannot be obtained lawfully to measure. What the set does cover is a wide
 * range of ways to write a sentence, which is what it is for.
 */

export interface ReferenceWork {
  author: string;
  title: string;
  year: number;
  /** Loose, and only to spread the sample — not a claim about the book. */
  kind: string;
  /** Words measured, after the front and back matter were trimmed away. */
  words: number;
  /**
   * Whether what was measured is a translator's English rather than the
   * author's. Kept, because the prose is still prose and still various, but
   * flagged: nothing about Homer's sentences survives into a count of a
   * translation of them.
   */
  translated?: boolean;
  dialogueShare: number;
  features: Record<string, number>;
}

export const REFERENCE_WORKS: ReferenceWork[] =
